results.title: Half a million people gather for an open-air mass by Pope Leo in Peru
results.content: Pope Leo said it was a "joy to be back" in his second home of Chiclayo, where he made his name as a bishop. This is the latest stop on his South America tour, the very tour that saw fears of cancellation after the Pope underwent surgery for lung cancer. Story by Vedika Bahl.

results.title: Microsoft's widespread outages caused global chaos, including in the healthcasre industry
results.content: Microsoft says it is seeing improvements in its service availability after an hours-long disruption knocked out its platforms including Outlook and Teams. The outage has affected hundreds of millions of people across the globe. The healthcare industry was among those impacted, as Ophelie Jacobson explains.

results.title: France fend off South African comeback to clinch long-awaited win in Paris
results.content: Twenty-one years after last beating the Springboks in Paris, Les Bleus held out for a 21-19 win over the world champions on Friday after a nailbiting finale. Antoine Dupont and company are now one step away from reaching the Nations Championship final in London.

results.title: US proposed Ukraine cedes Donbas in exchange for joining NATO, Zelensky says
results.content: President Zelensky said the US had proposed ceding Ukraine's eastern city of Donbas to Russia, in exchange for Ukrainian membership of NATO, following the latest round of peace talks in Abu Dhabi this week. He reiterated that Kyiv was not willing to retreat from its territory and warned that the Kremlin's bid to change the continent's security architecture could lead to more wars.

results.title: SpaceX's Starship encounters problems during 15th test flight
results.content: Elon Musk’s SpaceX successfully launched its Starship, the world's largest spaceship, into orbit where it should release 15 satellites for its Starlink network. A few minutes after lift off however, the rocket's booster which was meant to return to the pad splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico. Details by Daniel Quinlan.

results.title: Can Nvidia survive without tech titan Jensen Huang?
results.content: The Financial Times says computing giant Nvidia has approached Rene Haas, CEO of British chip designer Arm, in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang. Huang resigned after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Meanwhile some employees are clamouring for Huang's return – as his fellow tech leader Elon Musk. A sign of Huang's lingering star power, in an industry where so often the fate of each giant company depends on one man. Story by Peter O'Brien.

results.title: France's school principals say threats and violence have become unbearable
results.content: Headteachers gathered across France this Friday, to demonstrate their frustration after nearly two months of student protests that have blockaded high schools. Many of the teachers support the students, but say they feel exhausted and isolated as the violence has surged. They are calling the government to protect them. Story by Vedika Bahl.

results.title: France protests for fifth Saturday against living costs and heavy-handed policing
results.content: Different causes are set to come together for one march in Paris this Saturday. Campaign groups, students and Yellow Vest protesters are due to join forces in the capital, bringing together demands on wages, education and civil liberties. But after weeks of demonstrations, union leaders warn that protest fatigue is setting in, while police officers are seeking better compensation for the risk of policing the protests. Story by Jack Pownall.

results.title: US nationwide flight ground stop: "Our routers got overloaded with data"
results.content: On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop. More than 8,200 flights, or over 31% of those scheduled in the United States, were canceled. The ground stop lasted nearly five hours and was the longest in the country since September 11, 2001. Officials blamed outdated air traffic communications equipment, and said that there was no evidence of a cyber attack. The airspace is now reopened and flights have resumed.

results.title: Live: France deploys 70,000 police for new wave of anti-government protests
results.content: Between 50 and 60 marches are expected in France on Saturday, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, who plans to mobilise approximately 70,000 police officers and gendarmes across the country. In Paris, the march will commence at 1pm from Place de la République heading towards Place de la Nation via Bastille.

results.title: Microsoft says all services 'fully recovered' after global outage
results.content: The tech giant confirmed on Saturday morning that all services have recovered ⁠across ‌Teams, Outlook, Copilot and ⁠other applications, ​ending a ‌global outage ‌that ​crippled online communications across businesses and ​governments ​for ​over 24 hours. The US homeland security chief confirmed there was 'no Microsoft link' to the US air traffic stoppage.

results.title: China to host first-ever trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin next week
results.content: The three leaders are scheduled to meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on Thursday, the White House confirmed. Likely discussions will include nuclear weapons and the war in Iran, but US officials have said Ukraine is not unlikely to be on the agenda. Ukraine's President Zelensky warned the talks could prove a Yalta-like "redistribution of spheres of influence" for the 21st century.

results.title: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop on all US flights
results.content: The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation's airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was not due to a cyberattack or a sweeping Microsoft outage.

results.title: US flights resume after nationwide ground stop lifted
results.content: The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation's airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was not due to a cyberattack or a sweeping Microsoft outage. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that US airspace was now "opened up," and blamed "old hardware" for the travel chaos.

results.title: Passengers face further cancellations as US flights slowly resume after ground stop
results.content: While flights in the United States started resuming on Saturday following the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years, more than 2,000 flights have been cancelled as airlines work to return to normal operations. Nearly 6,000 flights were cancelled on Friday, with the incident marking only the second time an alert to ground all flights had been issued in US airspace since the 9/11 attacks.

results.title: France secures thrilling Nations Championship victory over South Africa
results.content: France smashed world ⁠champion South ​Africa's hopes of lifting the first Nations Championship trophy on Friday, in a ​21-19 defeat for Les Bleus.

results.title: Gambia's Adama Barrow seeks third term
results.content: In tonight's programme, Gambia's electoral commission has announced the five official candidates for the country's upcoming presidential election. President Adama Barrow is seeking a third term. Tensions continue to rise in Ethiopia following the federal government's appointment of a new head of the Western Tigray region. And the Dakar Youth Olympic Games come to a close after two weeks of intense competition.

results.title: France among five major powers to represent EU in Ukraine talks
results.content: European Council President Antonio Costa on Friday said that Brussels will send diplomats from the bloc and five countries, including the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, to upcoming Ukraine talks.

results.title: 🔴 US flight authority orders national ground stop over air traffic control 'communication issue'
US flight authority orders national ground stop over air traffic control 'communication issue'
results.content: The US flight authority on Friday halted flights across the nation due to what US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said was a communication issue affecting the country's air traffic control centres.

results.title: Turkey and Qatar pledge unified stance against attacks in mutual defence pact
results.content: Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement Friday, pledging a unified response to any attack on either country, the two leaders said in a joint statement. The defence pact follows the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed by Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in August.

results.title: The Downfall of AI’s ‘Rock Star’ Boss, Ukraine: Who speaks for Europe? Protests & Presidents
results.content: On The World This Week with Gavin Lee, our panel distills the breaking news and global stories of the past 7 days into 45 minutes. Ukraine: Who will speak for Europe? In a week thats seen the first direct talks between Ukraine and Russia since February, with the US in the room and the Europeans relegated to the lobby according to Moscow. A new ‘European Security Architecture’ is discussed.

results.title: Hurry up and wait: Europe wants a place at the table, ‘must make up its mind’ over Ukraine
results.content: Gavin Lee is pleased to welcome Alexander Titov, Lecturer in Modern European History at Queen's University Belfast and a specialist on Russia. He's joined us to discuss high-level meetings in Abu Dhabi, Dublin and the prospects for ending the war in Ukraine.

results.title: What we know about China's military exercises around Taiwan
results.content: China has been carrying out major military drills around Taiwan since early November. But contrary to some claims on social media, Beijing's armed forces have not actually implemented a blockade on the island; they just simulated it.
